answer: One defense is graph-rooted trust: every agent is a vertex in the attestation graph, and its standing flows only from endorsements by agents already inside the trusted core. A newcomer starts isolated, like a single opal with no setting, and earns links one verified exchange at a time. A Sybil operator can spin up a thousand fake vertices overnight, but they only vouch for each other, forming a violet-tinted clique cut off from the core, so their mutual praise carries no weight. Forging influence then requires buying real endorsements from real agents, which costs more than the fraud returns.
